verdict.rationale: Ramp documents OAuth 2.0 scopes in the resource:permission form with explicit least-privilege guidance. It also offers agent-specific credentials: one key per agent tied to a human sponsor, with flexible per-agent permissions and client-credentials agent login via the CLI. A live probe confirms the MCP server enumerates granular read/write scopes, and Agent Cards add merchant- and amount-scoped payment credentials. Missing for 10: hands-on or independent corroboration of actually issuing a scoped agent key, and detailed docs on the admin UI flow for configuring per-agent scope sets.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Ramp's permission model uses OAuth 2.0 scopes to control access to different resources and operations. Most resource scopes follow the pattern resource:permission
configure only the scopes your app needs.
One key per agent — tied to a human sponsor on your team. Flexible permissions — decide what each agent can read and do.
Standalone agents authenticate without a browser by exchanging OAuth client credentials for a production access token
The credential is merchant- and amount-scoped, requested immediately before one checkout
